newsitem.title: USA: Alcan Aluminium CEO calls for EU to lift tariff.
newsitem.headline: Alcan Aluminium CEO calls for EU to lift tariff.

text.p: The president and chief executive officer of Alcan Aluminium Ltd said Monday that the European Union's six percent tariff on imports of primary aluminum is a "clear distortion of trade" and makes European products less competitive in world markets.

Speaking to the Canadian-American Business Council, Jacques Bougie said he has not proposed that the U.S. and Canada offer anything in exchange for a potential lifting of the EU duty but said in response to a question that he did not believe such a quid pro quo action would be necessary.
"Our view is that the tariff should not be there," said Bougie.
Bougie also said it was important that Russia be admitted to the World Trade Organization to make sure Russia adheres to the rules of the marketplace.

"It is important for the aluminum industry in particular, that Russian exports be subject to the rules and regimes of the marketplace. Among other things, the WTO protects its members against unfair trade practices such as dumping."
A huge jump in Russian aluminum exports last year caused aluminum prices to drop. According to Bougie, aluminum is now Russia's largest source of hard cash, after oil exports.
Bougie said the auto industry holds potential promise for the aluminum industry, and predicted that the car industry will be aluminum's highest gorwth industry for the next 40 years.
